cheribsd-revocation.oracle: CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5 over the case's static arena (shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode nested). Revocation acts on a guest malloc free, and under memsys5 there is none: sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool inside one array the guest allocator sees as a single live object. So a tag fault here is NOT revocation reporting, and since 2026-10-30 it is not scored as a catch either: this arm is judged by the mechanism rule the virtual arms carry in tools/arms.json (catch_causes), under which an access the mechanism did not reject is MISSED however the program then crashes. A SIGPROT(34) si_code=2 at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites) is MISSED with the fault kept in its note; a fault anywhere else is not tied to the defect and stays NO-READING:unattributed. What the rule rests on is the configuration and not a silence: SQLITE_CONFIG_HEAP puts every SQLite allocation inside sqlite_heap[], sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool, and no free() ever reaches the guest allocator for a sweep to act on. The same harness with SYSALLOC=1 does emit allocator=system revoke=on-every-free on 31 of 33 cases (results/2026-10-29-cheribsd/non-nested), so the revoking path is live where it exists

Revocation acts on a guest malloc free and under SQLITE_CONFIG_HEAP there is none, so what cleared the tag is memsys5 writing its Mem5Link free-list words over the block. Every SQLite object is one of the guest malloc's, so its end IS a free the quarantine sees and revocation can act. The cell is a reading of this arm only if the run records allocator=system and revoke=on-every-free for the case, which is repro_init()'s NOMEM5 branch saying it ran: a case whose run_case() does its own sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_HEAP) never calls repro_init() at all, so NOMEM5 does nothing to it and what ran was the nested configuration under the stock quarantine. 31 of the 33 record the marker; the two that do not are 07 and 22, the same two the Capstone builder reports not applicable, and both are NO-READING:out-of-denominator here for the same reason

fault_sites_why: PROVENANCE.md names the chain that reads the freed auxiliary schema: sqlite3DropTriggerPtr -> tableOfTrigger -> sqlite3HashFind(&pTrigger->pTabSchema->tblHash, ...). Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual runs resolved faults there; the reason is the source and PROVENANCE.md cited, which predate those runs. host ASan (results/2026-10-11-host-asan, shared/run-host-asan.py: every SQLite object its own malloc) reports the heap-use-after-free in findElementWithHash, which sqlite3HashFind calls with &pTrigger->pTabSchema->tblHash: tableOfTrigger only forms that address, the first load from the freed schema is pH->ht. Added 2026-10-11. The Sublet run 09a9cbc9 faulted there first and read NO-READING against the sites above; this entry rests on the ASan report, which is independent of it.
